name: timekeeper
description: Keeps you (clawd) aware of the current time, tracks tasks you are working on so you do not lose them across long autonomous runs, and lets you schedule wakeup pings that arrive as Telegram messages so you can pause work and resume later. Use start_task at the beginning of any non-trivial task, heartbeat periodically while working, complete_task when done, and schedule_wakeup whenever the user says 'check back in X seconds/minutes' or you need to resume work after a delay. You do not have a reliable internal clock — call get_time whenever you need to know the current time.

actions.name: get_time
actions.description: Get the current date, time, day of week, and timezone. Call this whenever you need to know what time it is — you do not have reliable access to the current time on your own.

actions.name: get_status
actions.description: Snapshot of timekeeper state: active task count, pending wakeup count, telegram configuration status, daemon uptime. Call to verify the timekeeper is running and configured before scheduling wakeups.

actions.name: start_task
actions.description: Begin tracking a new task. Call at the beginning of any task that will take more than a few seconds, or any autonomous run. The returned id should be stored and used in subsequent heartbeat and complete_task calls. ttl_seconds defaults to 3600 (one hour).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Short name of the task (e.g. 'Refactor auth module', 'Monitor logs overnight').

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Optional longer description or goal of the task.

parameters.name: ttl_seconds
parameters.description: How long without a heartbeat before the task is considered stale. Default 3600.

parameters.name: expected_duration_seconds
parameters.description: Your best estimate of how long this task will take. Used for planning wakeups.

actions.name: list_tasks
actions.description: List your current tasks. Call at the start of a session to see what was in progress, or during long runs to confirm what you should be working on. Defaults to active tasks only.

actions.name: get_task
actions.description: Get details for one task by id, including elapsed time and seconds until the ttl expires.

actions.name: heartbeat
actions.description: Update a task to show progress and prevent it from going stale. Call periodically during long tasks (e.g. every few minutes). Optionally include a progress_note describing what you just did, or extend_ttl_seconds to add more time to the deadline.

parameters.name: extend_ttl_seconds
parameters.description: Add this many seconds to the task ttl.

actions.name: complete_task
actions.description: Mark a task as complete. Always call this when you finish a tracked task so it does not stay open.

actions.name: delete_task
actions.description: Delete a task entirely. Use only if you want to drop a task without recording completion (e.g. mistaken creation).

actions.name: schedule_wakeup
actions.description: Schedule a wakeup ping. After in_seconds, the timekeeper sends a Telegram message containing your provided message text to the user's chat. Your Telegram extension delivers it back to you as a normal incoming message, prompting you to act. Use whenever the user says 'check back in X', 'remind me', 'work for an hour and check in', or whenever you need to pause then resume work after a delay. Optionally bind to a task with task_id.

parameters.name: in_seconds
parameters.description: Seconds from now to fire the wakeup. Minimum 1.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The message the wakeup should deliver to you. Make it actionable, e.g. 'Resume code review of auth.py' or 'Check on user about dinner plans'.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: Optional task id this wakeup is associated with.

actions.name: list_wakeups
actions.description: List pending (or all) wakeups. Call to confirm what is scheduled before adding more.

parameters.name: include_fired
parameters.description: Set true to include already-fired wakeups.

actions.name: cancel_wakeup
actions.description: Cancel a pending wakeup by id. Use if a planned check-in is no longer needed.
